articles.title: Pannun’s civil lawsuit: U.S. State Department formally serves notice on India
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: The U.S. State Department, through a diplomatic note, has formally served notice on the Government of India regarding Khalistan separatist Gurpatwant Pannun’s civil lawsuit over an alleged assassination plot.

The U.S. State Department said it was legally obliged to do so and is not taking a position on the case, adding, “The documents were delivered to the Embassy of India in Washington under cover of the U.S. Department of State note dated October 20, 2026. The diplomatic note was signed on September 30, 2026, and delivered on October 9, 2026.”

The U.S. State Department’s diplomatic note said “I, John Ballard Managing Director of the Directorate of Overseas Citizens Services, in Washington certify that this is a true copy of the United States Department of State diplomatic note signed on September 30, 2026 and delivered to the Embassy of the Republic of India in Washington DC on October 9, 2026.”

On February 16, 2026, Indian citizen Nikhil Gupta had pled “guilty” at a court in New York to charges of murder, conspiracy, and money laundering to assassinate Khalistani activist Gurpatwant Singh Pannun. The government is yet to comment on the case.

According to investigators in the United States, Mr. Gupta, an Indian businessman, worked with an Indian “government employee” Vikash Yadav, believed to have been associated with India’s external intelligence agency R&AW, to hire a hitman to carry out Mr. Pannun’s murder for a total sum of $100,000. Mr. Yadav, who was arrested in December 2023 in Delhi in a separate case of kidnapping and extortion, has been out on bail since April 2024.

articles.title: Hyderabad gears up for Chhath Puja from November 13-16, 2026
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: While Deepavali marks the culmination of the festive celebrations for many communities across India, people from Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, Jharkhand and parts of West Bengal are preparing for another important festival — Chhath Puja . This year, large numbers of devotees are expected to gather at lakes, ponds and other water bodies across Hyderabad to offer prayers to the setting and rising Sun.

Ahead of the celebrations, the Telangana government has directed civic bodies and disaster management authorities to facilitate Chhath Puja at 28 locations across the city and make necessary arrangements, including sanitation, lighting, drinking water and crowd management. In a recent memo, the Municipal Administration and Urban Development (MAUD) department has forwarded the association’s representation to the Hyderabad Disaster Response and Asset Protection Agency (HYDRAA), and the three municipal corporations asking them to take necessary action in coordination with the departments concerned.

Chhath Puja is dedicated to the worship of the Sun God (Surya) and Chhathi Maiya. The Sun is worshipped as the source of life, energy and sustenance. Devotees offer prayers to the setting and rising Sun, seeking good health, prosperity, happiness and the well-being of their families.
Devotees offer prayers to the setting and rising Sun during Chhath Puja festival. File | Photo Credit: NAGARA GOPAL

Chhath Puja is a four-day festival, with each day having a distinct ritual. The first day, Nahay Khay, involves devotees taking a ritual bath, cleaning their homes and preparing a traditional meal. The second day, Kharna, involves a day-long fast, which is broken after sunset with offerings such as jaggery-based kheer, chapati and fruits. Following this, devotees undertake a rigorous fast without food and water.

On the third day, known as Sandhya Arghya, devotees gather at rivers, lakes, ponds and other water bodies to offer prayers to the setting Sun. Standing in water, they make offerings of fruits, sugarcane and traditional preparations. The festival concludes on the fourth day with Usha Arghya, when devotees return to the water bodies before sunrise to offer prayers to the rising Sun. The rituals conclude with devotees breaking their fast.
Chhath Puja is a four-day festival — Nahay Khay, Kharna, Sandhya Arghya and Usha Arghya — with each day having a distinct ritual. File | Photo Credit: NAGARA GOPAL

The celebrations in Hyderabad — organised by the Bihar Association, Hyderabad — are scheduled for November 14, 15 and 16. The proposed locations fall under the Greater Hyderabad Municipal Corporation (GHMC), Cyberabad Municipal Corporation (CMC) and Malkajgiri Municipal Corporation (MMC) limits. Some of the proposed locations include Tank Bund, Hasmatpet Lake, Durgam Cheruvu, Shamirpet, Miyapur and Uppal, among several others.

The association has proposed celebrations at 28 specifically named locations, apart from other Bathukamma ghats in and around the city. Tank Bund is expected to be among the major gathering points for the celebrations. “The biggest location which sees huge crowds is the Bathukamma Ghat at Tank Bund, where thousands of devotees gather to celebrate the puja. Many Ministers, legislators and retired and serving bureaucrats also participate in the celebrations here,” said Bihar Association president Hareram Singh.

The Bihar Association has urged the civic bodies to clean and maintain the designated ghats and surrounding areas, with particular attention to sanitation and hygiene. It has also sought adequate lighting at the ghats and approach roads, drinking water facilities and other essential public amenities. With devotees expected to gather for the evening prayers on November 15 and the morning rituals on November 16, the association has specifically requested adequate lighting during these periods.

Other requests include crowd management and traffic regulation in coordination with the Police Department, provision of chairs, carpets and mats, public-address systems and, wherever necessary, stages or platforms to facilitate the organised conduct of the celebrations. The association has also sought necessary safety and civic arrangements to ensure that devotees can perform the rituals in a safe, clean and orderly environment.

articles.title: Andhra government expected to make significant allocations for Neradi barrage to be constructed on Vamsadhara river
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Andhra Pradesh government is expected to make allocations in the next annual budget of the State for the year 2027-28 for the construction of Neradi barrage across Vamsadhara River and ensure dedicated water facility for nearly 2.56 lakh acres of lands in Srikakulam district of AP, which has waited nearly 55 years to overcome water dispute with the neighbouring Odisha State.

According to BRR Vamsadhara Project Chairman Aravala Ravindrababu, the State government which had given an administrative sanction for ₹461 crores a couple of months back, may give additional sanctions in the next budget. “On the request from Union Minister for Civil Aviation K. Rammohan Naidu, the Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu is keen to complete Neradi barrage within a couple of years. As a first step, it has given administrative sanction to ensure compensation for land acquisition and other needs,” said Mr. Ravindrababu while speaking to The Hindu .

Six days ago, the AP government proposed this project for optimum utilisation of water of Vamsadhara which flows nearly 82 km across Srikakulam district after flowing across 154 km in Odisha from its origin in Kalahandi district of neighbouring State. However, it was not taken up as 106 acres of land in Odisha had to be acquired for this project.

Vamsadhara Water Disputes Tribunal, which was appointed to oversee the issue, has asked AP to pay compensation for the land in Odisha and construct the project. Although the order was given in the year 2021, the Union Ministry of Water Resources has not given its nod for the project till the intervention of Mr. Chandrababu Naidu and Mr. Rammohan Naidu. As the Centre had given a notification recently, AP is all set to take up the project which might need around ₹1,099 crores. The initial allocation of ₹461 crore would ensure completion of land acquisition and beginning of the works. Mr. Ravindrababu said that the project would help farmers to grow three crops in a year in several mandals including Bhamini, Amudalavalasa, Srikakulam, Narasannapeta and others.

articles.title: Strait of Hormuz LNG traffic hits highest in October since Iran war began
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: The monthly tally of laden liquefied natural gas (LNG) tankers exiting the ​Strait of Hormuz reached its highest in October since ‌the U.S.-Iran conflict disrupted shipping this year, vessel ​tracking data showed.

* Last month, ⁠31 LNG tankers went through the key waterway, according to data from S&P Global Energy, of which ‌23 were loaded at Ras Laffan in Qatar and eight at Das Island ‌in the United Arab Emirates.
* October exports ‌were ⁠the highest since February when the war ⁠started and were up from September’s corresponding tally of 23 vessels exiting the strait, the data showed.
* “We are ​looking at UAE ‌back to pre-war transit levels and Qatar at over 30% of pre-war Hormuz transits,” said Eric Yep, a senior principal analyst at ‌S&P Global Energy.
* Kpler’s shiptracking data showed ​42 LNG cargoes were loaded in October, up from 27 in September.

* ⁠The changes come as Ras Laffan’s October loadings reached 35 cargoes, surpassing 2.7 million tons, the ‌highest since the war started, according to Kpler data. Qatar exported nearly 6.2 million tons in February.

* Two of the vessels carrying LNG from Ras Laffan that exited the strait subsequently conducted ship-to-ship (STS) transfers off the coast of ‌Oman’s Sohar anchorage, Kpler data showed. The SC Prestige ​transferred LNG to the BW ENN Crystal Sky, which is now bound for ⁠South Korea.
* The Al Mafyar moved its LNG ⁠to Shandong Redwood and Ejnan, both of which delivered the cargoes to Pakistan.
* ‌Das Island exports held steady at seven loadings in October, flat with September, Kpler ​data showed.

articles.title: RBI extends Abhyudaya Bank supersession by another year
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has extended the supersession of the board of Mumbai-based Abhyudaya Co-operative Bank Ltd. by another year, effective November 24, 2026, citing public interest.

“Upon a review, the Reserve Bank of India is satisfied that, in the public interest, it is necessary to further extend the period of supersession beyond the close of business of the bank as on November 23, 2026,” the RBI said in a circular.
The RBI first superseded the bank’s Board of Directors for one year on November 24, 2023, citing “material concerns arising from poor governance standards observed within the bank.”
The supersession, initially imposed for a year, has since been extended annually, first in November 2024, again in November 2025 and now for a further year from November 24, 2026.

With the latest extension, Mr. Satya Prakash Pathak will continue as the bank’s Administrator. He will be assisted by the existing Committee of Advisors comprising Mr. Venkatesh Hegde, Mr. Devendra Kumar and Mr. Suhas Gokhale.

articles.title: OALP deepwater bidding deadline extended again to December 10
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: The Directorate General of Hydrocarbons (DGH) on Monday extended the deadline for submitting bids for deepwater and ultra-deepwater blocks under the 10th and 11th rounds of the Open Acreage Licensing Policy (OALP) by 25 days to December 10.

The latest extension marks the seventh for the 10th round, launched in April last year, and the third for the 11th round, which opened in March this year. The deadlines were last extended in September by nearly two months to November 15.
The 10th round offers 25 blocks, including one deepwater and 12 ultra-deepwater blocks, while the 11th round has five blocks on offer, comprising one deepwater and four ultra-deepwater areas.

In August, the Union Cabinet approved an outlay of ₹84,084 crore for the Petroleum Ministry’s National Offshore Exploration Scheme, titled ‘Samudra Manthan’. The corpus, to be utilised until FY31, includes ₹43,200 crore for drilling 60 deepwater and ultra-deepwater wells.

State-owned explorers ONGC and Oil India have also announced substantial investments in offshore exploration. ONGC plans to invest ₹1 lakh crore by 2030, while Oil India has earmarked ₹15,000 crore over the next three years for deepwater and ultra-deepwater exploration.

articles.title: Oil falls as Donald Trump says new Iran attacks ‘unlikely’
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: Oil prices fell at Monday’s (November 9, 2026) open after U.S. President ​Donald Trump said he was highly unlikely to order new Iran ‌attackswhile talks to end the conflict make progress, despite both ​nations’ reports of attacks on ships in or near ⁠the Strait of Hormuz.
Brent was down 84 cents, or 0.85%, to $97.48 a barrel by 0138 GMT, while West Texas Intermediate fell 32 cents, or ‌0.35%, to $90.51 a barrel.

The fall reversed minor gains made on Friday’s (November 6, 2026) settlement as the market assessed the ‌possibility of further U.S. strikes on Iran, although Brent fell ‌17% ⁠last week, the steepest weekly drop since the start ⁠of the COVID pandemic and the biggest in absolute terms, according to LSEG data dating back to 1988.

articles.title: Explosions heard in Saudi capital Riyadh: AFP journalists
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: Multiple explosions were heard in the Saudi capital on Tuesday (November 10, 2026), as the military coalition fighting Yemen's Houthis said it had intercepted a ballistic missile launched by the Iran-backed group towards Riyadh.
AFP journalists heard the blasts and residents received an alert on their mobile phones instructing them to take shelter due to an "aerial threat".
"Air defences intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile launched by the terrorist Houthi militia towards Riyadh," the Saudi-led coalition posted on X.
A subsequent message from the country's civil defence agency said the danger had passed.
The coalition had earlier said air defences also destroyed a ballistic missile headed towards the southern region overnight.
Saudi Arabia, the world's biggest oil exporter, has faced near-daily strikes from the Houthis for weeks, after a truce in their long-running conflict unravelled in July.
On Sunday (November 8), the Houthis claimed attacks on Riyadh's business district, where witnesses said the Aramco Tower was damaged.
Saudi authorities said the building suffered minor damage from falling shrapnel after an "attempted attack".

Images released by Saudi Arabia's press agency on Tuesday (November 10) showed the Riyadh region's deputy governor and other officials inspecting the building, with visible damage to some of its floors.
The Houthis have repeatedly targeted Aramco tankers, refineries, storage areas and the company's headquarters.
The coalition has in response been launching airstrikes against Houthi positions inside Yemen.

According to Houthi news agency Saba, Saudi warplanes on Tuesday (November 10) carried out a series of strikes on the capital Sanaa and its outskirts, targeting a gas facility and a building belonging to the Yemeni state oil company.

articles.title: Pannun’s civil lawsuit: U.S. State Department formally serves notice on India
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: The U.S. State Department, through a diplomatic note, has formally served notice on the Government of India regarding Khalistan separatist Gurpatwant Pannun’s civil lawsuit over an alleged assassination plot.

The U.S. State Department said it was legally obliged to do so and is not taking a position on the case, adding, “The documents were delivered to the Embassy of India in Washington under cover of the U.S. Department of State note dated October 20, 2026. The diplomatic note was signed on September 30, 2026, and delivered on October 9, 2026.”

The U.S. State Department’s diplomatic note said “I, John Ballard Managing Director of the Directorate of Overseas Citizens Services, in Washington certify that this is a true copy of the United States Department of State diplomatic note signed on September 30, 2026 and delivered to the Embassy of the Republic of India in Washington DC on October 9, 2026.”

On February 16, 2026, Indian citizen Nikhil Gupta had pled “guilty” at a court in New York to charges of murder, conspiracy, and money laundering to assassinate Khalistani activist Gurpatwant Singh Pannun. The government is yet to comment on the case.

According to investigators in the United States, Mr. Gupta, an Indian businessman, worked with an Indian “government employee” Vikash Yadav, believed to have been associated with India’s external intelligence agency R&AW, to hire a hitman to carry out Mr. Pannun’s murder for a total sum of $100,000. Mr. Yadav, who was arrested in December 2023 in Delhi in a separate case of kidnapping and extortion, has been out on bail since April 2024.

articles.title: How China gets the Nvidia chips it needs to develop AI
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has admitted to having an affair, reportedly with a Chinese executive at a Singapore-based company that the United States suspects of smuggling AI microchips into China.
The scandal has focused attention on how China, a major artificial-intelligence power in itself, obtains the cutting-edge chips despite US export restrictions.
Nvidia designs advanced components originally created to handle 3D visuals in video games, called Graphics Processing Units (GPUs).
These have the power to crunch colossal amounts of digital data, so are also used at scale to train and run artificial intelligence.
ChatGPT's 2022 launch showcased the potential of AI, sparking an investment gold rush as governments and tech giants raced to develop the technology further.
With chip orders pouring in, Nvidia's market valuation has soared to $4.5 trillion -- currently on par with Apple as the world's two most valuable companies.
Washington bans the export of Nvidia's top-end "Blackwell" and "Rubin" GPUs to China, citing security concerns, as advanced AI has military applications.
The policy also allows the United States's top AI labs to maintain their global lead.
Huang has lobbied the U.S. government to allow Nvidia chip sales to China, warning that the restrictions are fuelling the rise of competitive homegrown alternatives.
This year, Washington eased controls on Nvidia's previously banned -- and less powerful -- "H200" chip, with the United States taking a 25% cut of sales.
But U.S. conditions have made it difficult for shipments to be approved, with Beijing also reportedly reluctant to buy H200s as its own chip industry gains momentum.
Recent launches of high-performing models from Chinese startups, including Moonshot AI, Z.ai and DeepSeek, have turned up the heat on U.S. rivals.

articles.title: What are the eight Articles of impeachment filed against U.S. Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth?
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: There is a major shift happening in Capitol Hill following the U.S. midterm elections, as Representative Thomas Massie supported by lawmakers, including Representative Ro Khanna, introduced eight Articles of impeachment against U.S. Secretary of Defence Pete Hegseth.
The Articles cite violations of the 1973 War Powers Resolution, alongside misconduct involving civilian casualties and operations in Yemen and Venezuela.

Mr. Hegseth, a former Fox News weekend host and one of President Donald Trump’s handpicked appointees in his second term as U.S. President, took charge of the Department of War despite lacking administrative experience commensurate with the post. Despite controversies surrounding his tenure, Mr. Trump has maintained his support and repeatedly dismissed suggestions of dismissing him.
Here is the complete breakdown of the eight Articles of impeachment introduced in the formal House resolution.
Article 1 charges Mr. Hegseth with executing unlawful military orders by launching hostilities against Iran on February 28, 2026.

The resolution states that the military strikes violated Section 2(c) of the 1973 War Powers Resolution because Congress had not declared war, provided statutory authorisation or faced any national emergency caused by an attack by the Islamic Republic of Iran against the U.S.

Article II focuses on Mr. Hegseth’s refusal to comply with Congress’s directive to withdraw U.S. forces from Iran. After both the House and Senate passed House Concurrent Resolution 86 (the first successful passage of such a legislative vehicle by both chambers of Congress in the history of the United States of America) to end unauthorised hostilities in June 2026, Mr. Hegseth allegedly directed the Department of Defence to ignore the resolution and continue with military strikes.

As per Section 5 (b) of the War Powers Resolution, authorised military action must terminate within 60 days (after a report is submitted or is required to be submitted to Congress). Article III alleges Mr. Hegseth continued conducting hostile military operations in Iran beyond the mandatory statutory deadlines of May 1 and June 1, 2026, without congressional extensions.

This Article accuses Mr. Hegseth of “cultivating a warmaking culture” and a “course of conduct that effected the systemic deterioration and removal of Department of Defence infrastructure that Congress had mandated by law to limit collateral damage to civilians and non-military objects during military operations”, among other allegations.
It specifically highlights the February 28, 2026, cruise missile strike on the Shajareh Tayyebeh Elementary School in Iran, which killed and wounded over 200 civilians, mostly children.

Article V targets a strike campaign against suspected narcotics smuggling vessels in international waters (in the Caribbean Sea and Eastern Pacific Ocean) that resulted in at least 221 deaths across 63 attack events.

It charges Mr. Hegseth with using lethal military force instead of standard maritime law enforcement framework (sections 102 and 522 of Title 14), lowering targeting standards, and ordering or permitting actions that denied quarter and failed to rescue shipwrecked survivors.

articles.title: Pete Hegseth to hold first Pentagon briefing since May amid impeachment threat
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth is scheduled to give his first news conference from the Pentagon in six months on Tuesday (November 10, 2026), just a day after a Republican lawmaker launched an effort to impeach him over his handling of the unpopular war against Iran and other actions.

The briefing will be Hegseth's first since May even as the U.S. military has kept up intermittent operations against the Islamic Republic as well as fatal strikes on alleged drug-smuggling boats in Latin America.

Mr. Hegseth, who has said the news conference would focus on the impeachment threat, is gearing up for a fight, having launched a social media blitz and saying he is ready to defend his and President Donald Trump's actions from “politically motivated people.”

Rep. Thomas Massie, a Kentucky Republican who lost his primary to a Trump-backed opponent, filed the impeachment resolution in the House on Monday (November 9). It sets the stage for a dramatic vote on whether to remove a prominent Trump administration figure following sweeping losses for Republicans in last week's midterm elections that many at least partly blamed on the Iran conflict and its economic impact.

The resolution largely focuses on the war in Iran but also includes references to Mr. Hegseth's role in military actions in Yemen against Iranian-backed Houthi rebels and Venezuela. Massie said Hegseth's actions amount to “high crimes and misdemeanors” and his leadership at the Pentagon “warrants impeachment.”
A vote in the House could come by midweek, putting pressure on Republicans — many of whom blamed their election wipeout on the Iran war — but next steps are highly uncertain.

Mr. Trump has backed Hegseth, pointing to the raid to capture then-Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro in January as well as military operations against Iran that he asserts have “obliterated” its navy and air force.

Iran, however, has been able to keep striking U.S. military bases in West Asia and has disrupted shipping in the Strait of Hormuz during the course of the more than 8-month-old conflict, driving up global oil prices. Mr. Trump told reporters on Monday (November 9) that the Iran war “militarily is effectively over" and repeated his often-made claim that Iran “would love to make a deal.”
Mr. Hegseth also has been defending his stewardship of the U.S. military.

“There's a lot of politically motivated people who may have substantial policy disagreements, but their disagreements are with success,” he told reporters on Monday (November 10) after a speech at the Naval War College in Rhode Island. He added that “if we want to litigate” the military actions that the Trump administration has taken, “I'm happy to do it all day long.”
He also released a video on social media last week that argued impeachment would be “all about the politics of personal destruction” and that “won't work with me. You can rest assured of that.”
Afterward, scores of Pentagon political appointees posted images of Hegseth emblazoned with the words, “Stand. Fight. Defend the Republic.”

articles.title: Republican Thomas Massie of Kentucky launches bid to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: Rep Thomas Massie on Monday (November 9, 2026) moved to force a vote to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, pressing his fellow Republicans to remove one of the Trump administration's most prominent figures following sweeping election losses blamed in part on fallout from the war in Iran.

Mr. Massie, a Kentucky Republican, read the impeachment resolution from the House floor just hours after it opened for the first day of sessions after the midterms. It largely focuses on the war in Iran but also includes references to Hegseth's role in carrying out military actions in Yemen and Venezuela.
The Congressman, who was defeated by a Trump-backed challenger in a primary earlier this year, said Mr. Hegseth's actions amounted to “high crimes and misdemeanors.”
Mr. Hegseth, he said, “knowingly executed and implemented unlawful orders” and “remains a threat to the Constitution.”
President Donald Trump lashed out at Massie personally just hours after the Congressman read the resolution, calling him a “loser” who “has a lot of hatred in his heart.”

A vote in the House could come by mid-week, but next steps are highly uncertain. House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries supports the measure. If most Democrats follow him, Mr. Massie would only need support from a few Republicans to impeach Hegseth.

If the House votes to impeach, it would fall to to the Senate to either dismiss the charges or hold a trial. Republicans remain in the majority in both chambers, until the new Congress convenes in January with Democrats in control.
Sen Chuck Schumer, the Democratic leader, endorsed the impeachment push. "Hegseth must stand trial before the Senate," he said.

Republican leaders, who are eager to use their final weeks in power executing their own agenda, expressed frustration at the move. House Speaker Mike Johnson, who has tried to prevent the vote, said impeachment “in the middle of hostilities abroad would be a terrible, terrible look, a terrible thing for our allies and our enemies to see that.”
Senate Majority Leader John Thune said he wasn't sure why the vote was being held now.
“We'll see what their ultimate decision is over there,” he said of the House. “We'll have to deal with it accordingly here."

Mr. Hegseth is stepping up his public statements ahead of the vote, telling reporters that he's eager to defend the military actions that he and Mr. Trump have taken against Iran, Yemen's Iranian-backed Houthi rebels and Venezuela's previous leaders.

articles.title: What is Megaspeed International, the firm under scanner over Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang affair
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: Megaspeed International, a Singapore-based cloud computing firm, is in the spotlight after the alleged extramarital affair of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang with one of the company’s former executives, Alice Huang. Ms Huang is accused of being a Chinese spy.

According to its website , Megaspeed is an Nvidia cloud partner in the Asia-Pacific region and a core business partner of Nvidia’s computing power cloud business. It adds that “we provide privatized, customized computing power product services covering NVIDIA’s entire GPU product line.”

A Reuters report says that Megaspeed International was incorporated in 2015 as 7Road International before changing its name to Megaspeed International in March 2023. It adds that the company is wholly owned by Singapore-registered Swiftdata, incorporated in October 2023, which says providing hosting services by non-data centers is its principal activity.

Reuters adds that Megaspeed’s assets increased sharply to $3 billion in 2024 from $33 million in 2023, its business filings showed. It reported an after-tax loss of $20 million ‌in ⁠2024, versus a loss of $21,283 a year earlier, while revenue jumped to $294 million from zero. Its cash flow statement showed $844,555 went to investing activities in 2024, after financing activities brought in cash of $10 million the previous year.

According to the company’s LinkedIn , it has around 2-10 employees and 23 associated members. The interactive map by LinkedIn shows that Megaspeed has offices in Iskandar Puteri, Malaysia; Senayan City, Indonesia; and is headquartered in the Central Region of Singapore.
Map showing the alleged locations of Megaspeed International | Photo Credit: Screengrab from LinkedIn

Washington has restricted the export of Nvidia’s most cutting-edge silicon chips to China, citing national security concerns. The move is also seen as a measure to stay ahead in the field of artificial intelligence.
The New York Times has reported that the U.S. government has been probing Megaspeed since 2024 over its potential steering of Nvidia chips to China.
All of this, combined with the allegations of Ms Huang being a Chinese spy, has triggered speculation over Megaspeed’s involvement in the alleged chip transfer to China.

As per an AFP report, in 2025, Bloomberg News also reported on the Singaporean probe into Megaspeed over the alleged smuggling of Nvidia chips to China. According to AFP , Megaspeed retorted in December of the same year, saying that Bloomberg’s reporting “contains misleading information and incorrect insinuations, including suggestions that we may have been involved in illegal chip transfers”.

Jensen Huang, the top boss of the chip maker and one of the world’s most valuable publicly traded companies, has admitted to being unfaithful to his wife, without disclosing details of the alleged relationship with Alice Huang. The Nvidia CEO said that he was “deeply sorry” for the affair. “I was unfaithful to my wife, my actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did,” the statement, uploaded on Nvidia’s website added.
The New York Times reported that Alice Huang is a Chinese citizen recruited by Beijing to collect intelligence on Jensen Huang.

articles.title: How China gets the Nvidia chips it needs to develop AI
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has admitted to having an affair, reportedly with a Chinese executive at a Singapore-based company that the United States suspects of smuggling AI microchips into China.
The scandal has focused attention on how China, a major artificial-intelligence power in itself, obtains the cutting-edge chips despite US export restrictions.
Nvidia designs advanced components originally created to handle 3D visuals in video games, called Graphics Processing Units (GPUs).
These have the power to crunch colossal amounts of digital data, so are also used at scale to train and run artificial intelligence.
ChatGPT's 2022 launch showcased the potential of AI, sparking an investment gold rush as governments and tech giants raced to develop the technology further.
With chip orders pouring in, Nvidia's market valuation has soared to $4.5 trillion -- currently on par with Apple as the world's two most valuable companies.
Washington bans the export of Nvidia's top-end "Blackwell" and "Rubin" GPUs to China, citing security concerns, as advanced AI has military applications.
The policy also allows the United States's top AI labs to maintain their global lead.
Huang has lobbied the U.S. government to allow Nvidia chip sales to China, warning that the restrictions are fuelling the rise of competitive homegrown alternatives.
This year, Washington eased controls on Nvidia's previously banned -- and less powerful -- "H200" chip, with the United States taking a 25% cut of sales.
But U.S. conditions have made it difficult for shipments to be approved, with Beijing also reportedly reluctant to buy H200s as its own chip industry gains momentum.
Recent launches of high-performing models from Chinese startups, including Moonshot AI, Z.ai and DeepSeek, have turned up the heat on U.S. rivals.

articles.title: Anthropic sends out, then retracts details of IPO filing, emails show
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: Details of Anthropic’s blockbuster IPO, ​including plans by the AI company to raise nearly $70 billion, were briefly ⁠circulated to banks before being retracted late on Monday, according to emails seen by Reuters.

A representative of Anthropic sent a copy of a securities filing that showed it aimed to sell about 867 ‌million shares at a price range of $70 to $80 per share, then followed up with an email saying details about the pricing were inaccurate. Anthropic said in ‌the second email it would update the filing later.
Anthropic declined to comment. The email ‌did ⁠not specify to bankers what was erroneous, and Reuters was unable to ⁠determine what was incorrect.

The original email whose details were retracted showed Anthropic planned to sell 866.7 million Class A shares, including a secondary offering. Anthropic itself would sell about 843.3 million shares, while existing shareholders would sell an additional ​23.3 million shares. The IPO would ‌raise $69.3 billion at the top of the range.

Separately, the original filing showed that Anthropic had lined up $26 billion in investments from some of the world’s biggest technology companies alongside its IPO, underscoring the increasingly intertwined financial ties underpinning the AI boom.

Alphabet’s Google, Nvidia, ‌Advanced Micro Devices, Broadcom, Micron Technology, Microsoft and TSMC had agreed to participate in the ​private placement of Anthropic’s Class N common stock at the IPO price, which would close immediately after the IPO, the original filing showed.
Anthropic is ⁠expected to formally launch the roadshow on Tuesday, with pricing expected in the following week.

The Anthropic IPO comes at a time when other companies in the AI infrastructure and data center ‌sectors have delayed or withdrawn their planned listings, facing a rise in interest rates that has helped fuel a punishing selloff in shares and bonds of AI operators such as CoreWeave Inc and broader questions about the sustainability of AI spending.

Investors had previously discussed a valuation of as much as $2 trillion for Anthropic, but expectations have since come down, with the $1.5 trillion figure viewed as the high end of the range, Reuters previously reported.

Founded in ‌2021 by former OpenAI executives including Amodei and his sister Daniela Amodei, who is now Anthropic’s president, Anthropic ​has emerged as one of the leading generative AI developers with its Claude family of models.

The company’s rapid growth has been underpinned by Google and ⁠Amazon, which are simultaneously investors, suppliers of computing power and important distribution partners, as well as ⁠AI competitors.

Anthropic had nearly $900 billion in computing commitments with partners including Amazon and Google, underscoring how its rapid growth depends on vast amounts of future capacity, some ‌of it reliant on financing beyond the company’s control.

articles.title: 331 tonnes of garbage removed from Madurai city after Deepavali
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: Madurai Corporation cleared a total of 331 tonnes of garbage, till 6 p.m. on Monday, which was generated across the city on Deepavali day.
Along with the corporation cleanliness workers, volunteers from the Democratic Youth Federation of India, joined the mass cleaning drive early on Monday morning.
Mayor (in-charge), T. Nagarajan, and Corporation Commissioner, Gaurav Kumar, inaugurated the cleanliness drive.

The drive started on the Chithrai Streets, Aavani Moola Streets, Masi Streets, Veli Streets and Vilakkuthoon junction around Sri Meenakshi Sundareswarar Temple where commercial establishments, especially textile showrooms, are located.
Besides, the workers focussed on spots at Teppakulam, Mattuthavani bus stand and Vaigai Bank Roads where garbage accumulation is higher.
Besides the usual vehicles used for transporting garbage, 11 earth movers, five bobcat machinery, nine tipper trucks and 42 tractors were involved in the exercise.

The work was expedited in the early hours so much so that 128.40 tonnes of garbage was cleared in the city by 12 noon. This was 33.32 tonnes of additional festival-time garbage removed when compared to 95.08 tonnes cleared during the same time in the last Deepavali season.
The workers had already removed 137 tonnes of garbage on Deepavali day (Sunday).
City Health Officer, Aravind Jothi, Assistant Health Officer, Abishek, DYFI district president, Selva, and secretary, Vel Deva, were present.

articles.title: Cracker conundrum: On need for strict enforcement of cracker ban
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: The two Deepavali nights following the Supreme Court’s (SC) temporary relaxation of the cracker ban , played out predictably. The Air Quality Index (AQI) in several north Indian cities — already ‘poor’ and ‘very poor’ in the first week of November — was ‘severe’ on Deepavali night . Several air sensors — maintained by various organisations — reported PM2.5 in Delhi and its outskirts, exceeding 1,000 by Deepavali night. In this context, the SC’s order last week regarding crackers bears revisiting. While stating it was aware of the consequences of emissions from crackers, the Court has been waiting for quantitative evidence on the health and environmental effects of emissions from Deepavali celebrations. Such direct, causative evidence is almost impossible to furnish. Slackening winds and post-monsoon atmospheric dryness are known to trap the latent particulate matter from vehicles, industries, construction dust and stubble burning. Crackers are only an additional element that further degrades an already vitiated air. Delhi’s five-day average AQI rose from approximately 298 before Deepavali to 358 afterwards in 2024, 259 to 315 in 2025 and from 350 to 376 in 2026. While the timing of these spikes is consistent with a contribution from firecrackers, their precise share of overall pollution cannot be isolated from other emissions and meteorological influences. An absolute ban would encourage “illegal crackers from across the border,” the Court was told. Cracker season begins a fortnight before Deepavali and therefore an earlier decision by the Court regarding its permissibility would have given stockists time to better dispense ‘green’ crackers.

However, it is important to note that CSIR-NEERI, the developers of the products, underline that low-emission crackers — under stringent lab conditions — only reduce emissions by 30%–45%. These percentage reductions reveal nothing about gross particulate matter emissions. The post-Deepavali AQI is evidence of this. The Court acknowledges, but does not address, the immense implementation challenges in policing cracker sales and hyphenates crackers with religious observation but pays only lip service to provisions in the Constitution that say that religious customs cannot override considerations of health and life. Rather than wait for the week running up to Deepavali 2027, the Court must pronounce a final view on crackers and lay down the contours for the government to evolve a policy on limiting the manufacture, sale, and burning of crackers in a time-bound manner.

articles.title: Point of no return: On Israel’s next government
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Israeli President Isaac Herzog’s decision to invite opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot to form the next government reflects the real mandate of the October 27 legislative elections. While Mr. Eisenkot’s centrist Yashar party finished second with 21 seats, behind Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s Likud, which won 27, the former military chief, who campaigned on an anti-Netanyahu platform, has secured the support of 67 legislators in the 120-member Knesset. In Mr. Eisenkot’s own words, Israel risks “descending to dark places, to a point of no return”. But it is not yet clear what kind of a government Mr. Eisenkot is seeking to form. The opposition parties are split between a Jewish-led bloc with 48 MKs and an Arab-led bloc of 19 MKs. Arab parties have offered in-principle support for Mr. Eisenkot to keep Mr. Netanyahu’s right-religious coalition out of power. But what is not clear is whether they would be part of the government or offer outside support by allowing Mr. Eisenkot to run a minority government. Some of Mr. Eisenkot’s Jewish right-wing allies, such as Avigdor Lieberman, are opposed to joining hands with Arab parties. Mr. Eisenkot has now called for a unity government, appealing even to Likud and the far-right Religious Zionism, to join him.

But the challenges facing Israel’s next leader are formidable and immediate. Mr. Netanyahu’s unchecked militarism has deepened Israel’s international isolation, strained its relationship with the U.S., its most important patron and ally, and aggravated the security challenges it faces in its neighbourhood. At home, the surge of the far-right has further polarised society, while systemic violence against Palestinians has spread across the West Bank. Mr. Netanyahu’s response to these challenges has been to unleash more violence, which has only compounded Israel’s problems. If Mr. Eisenkot is serious about pulling Israel back from the point of no return, he must pursue a three-pronged approach. Firstly, he should form an Arab-Jewish unity government focused on healing the country’s internal wounds and bridging gaps between communities. Second, Israel’s deepening international isolation and increasingly negative public opinion around the world will begin to exact a heavy toll sooner rather than later. Tel Aviv must take urgent steps to restore its international standing. Third, Israel must reopen the path to peace. The new government should initiate negotiations with the Palestinians under international mediation, crack down on settler violence, pull back from Gaza and reaffirm its commitment to the two-state solution. Without peace, Israel risks continuing to “descend to dark places”.

articles.title: Young and fast: on F1’s youngest champion
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Andrea Kimi Antonelli etched his name in motorsport history by becoming the youngest driver to win a Formula One World Championship . The 20-year-old has secured his maiden title with four races to spare after finishing third at the Mexico Grand Prix on Sunday. The Italian’s feat is remarkable, for he has claimed the crown in his sophomore campaign, becoming only the fifth driver in history to do so in the first or second season. Mercedes signed Antonelli for its junior driver programme when he was just 12. Since then, the Italian’s step towards F1 has been meticulously managed. After acing the F4 championships, Antonelli skipped one level to transition to F2. And when the opportunity arose to fill a seat vacated by seven-time champion Lewis Hamilton, Mercedes boss Toto Wolff took a bold gamble by drafting in the youngster. Antonelli’s rookie campaign in 2025 was baptism by fire, and he was outclassed by teammate George Russell. For 2026, F1 ushered in drastic changes with new engine and aerodynamic regulations, dramatically altering the dynamics of the cars. Though conventional wisdom suggested that the experienced Russell would be the favourite, the Italian prodigy embraced the challenge astonishingly well. This was best exemplified by how he won five consecutive races starting from the second round of the season.

One of the hardest things in F1 is handling the nerves associated with protecting the lead, especially when it is the driver’s first attempt at a Championship bid. Antonelli, though, was incredibly consistent throughout the year, and hardly made any errors. Titles are often decided by how a driver minimises his losses on bad days, and Antonelli showed great temperament in this regard. At the same time, he was ruthless on the track and made decisive overtaking manoeuvres. The defining race was in Monza, Italy, in September, where Antonelli charged from 19th on the grid to win his home Grand Prix, finishing ahead of Russell who started second. It was a statement of intent, and strengthened his grip on the trophy. Drivers often raise their games following a world title, more so when success comes early in their career. Considering the giant leap Antonelli made to become F1’s first champion to be born in the 21st century, he will undoubtedly attract a new generation of fans. The charm of the sport lies in its iconic driver rivalries such as Ayrton Senna versus Alain Prost, and Michael Schumacher versus Mika Hakkinen. With four-time champion Max Verstappen widely considered the gold standard of the present era, Antonelli could well be the perfect candidate to battle the Dutchman in F1’s next great rivalry.

articles.title: Epic failures: on electoral roll, welfare
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Union Panchayati Raj Minister Rajiv Ranjan Singh’s statement that voter identity cards, with biometric authentication, will replace Aadhaar as the basis for identifying beneficiaries and making payments under his Ministry’s schemes runs contrary to existing laws and regulations. Essentially, the electoral roll, prepared in several States through the flawed Special Intensive Revision (SIR) by the Election Commission of India (ECI), will become the dataset to vet the identities of beneficiaries. This contradicts the Supreme Court’s May 27 judgment on the Bihar SIR and its observations while hearing petitions against West Bengal’s orders removing people deleted during the SIR from the Public Distribution System and the Annapurna Yojana. The Court held that the ECI may undertake only a “limited enquiry” into citizenship to decide who belongs on the electoral roll, and that “any action taken pursuant thereto is confined to electoral consequences alone”. The consequence of deletion from the rolls, it said, is “correspondingly limited” to a person’s place on the roll and their right to vote. The Court also called the EPIC “a derivative document, issued on the basis of inclusion in the electoral roll”, and held that relying on it to verify that very roll would defeat the exercise. It is ironic that Mr. Singh now wants this “derivative document” to be the determinant of welfare benefits.

Not every citizen is an eligible voter, and tying benefits to the electoral roll is illogical and also cruel. In West Bengal, lakhs were deleted from the rolls , many for dubious “logical discrepancies”. In the appeals heard for reinstatement, 93% resulted in the restoration of names by September 2026, pointing to massive pre-election disenfranchisement. The Court has stated that it is yet to adjudicate on the legality of the ECI’s “logical discrepancies” method. The SIR was designed by the ECI to restrict enrolment through stringent residency criteria; thus, itinerant voters had to prove their eligibility. The Opposition, civil society and even some of the BJP’s allies have objected to this, but the BJP refuses to acknowledge the SIR’s flaws. This is partly because it has benefited from disenfranchisement — as in West Bengal. But the Minister’s remarks suggest another reason. The BJP-led coalition sees the pruned electoral rolls as a way to limit welfare, especially at a time when growth in tax revenues has slowed because of the Centre’s policies. Inordinately delaying the Census, changing the procedure to appoint Election Commissioners, who then run an exercise that disenfranchises millions by design, and now, using the resultant rolls to decide who gets welfare, all cut at the heart of the painstakingly built constitutional welfare state. The sooner the Court decides the petitions against the SIR, and reiterates that its rolls cannot be used to curtail welfare, the better.

articles.title: Trump debacle: On the U.S. midterm election results
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: President Donald Trump faced the worst political setback of his current term in office after the Republican Party lost control of both the Senate and the House of Representatives in the mid-term election. Democrats not only won resoundingly in their traditional stronghold States, such as Colorado, Oregon and Illinois, and held onto important swing States, such as Georgia, Michigan and Virginia, but they also made historic inroads into “red states” such as Texas, Kansas and Iowa. While Mr. Trump fumed that Republicans would have performed better had his name been on the ballot, he also appeared to be resigned to the imminent reality of working with Democratic lawmakers over the remaining two years of his administration. Beyond the immediate impact on the future functioning of the federal government, this week’s “bluenami” has also brought sweeping changes at the State level: Democrats won a Senate seat in Texas for the first time in 37 years; Democrat Abdul El-Sayed won in Michigan , making him the first Muslim Senator in history ; Chris Pappas of New Hampshire became the first openly gay man to be elected to the Senate ; and Senate Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries will soon be the first African-American Speaker of the House.
Federal judge orders 14-day delay on any work beginning on Trump’s monumental arch

It is ironic that Mr. Trump alluded to his name not being on the ballot as the cause for the Republican collapse because, for many voters, the midterm election was indeed a referendum on the second Trump administration’s performance in office. The result has been an unambiguous thumbs-down from voters so far as top policy areas of the Trump administration are concerned, including cost of living and jobs, immigration enforcement, the war in Iran. The writing was on the wall, as were the approval ratings, especially in the case of oil prices and the Iran war, given that the price of gas in the U.S. has soared since the conflict around the Strait of Hormuz escalated. Similarly, the widespread raids by ICE and accelerated deportation processes for undocumented migrants led to protests across States and galvanised progressives around immigration reform. While Democrats may be justified in celebrating their victory after two years of harsh Trumpism, they would do well to remember that the President still retains a veto vote for policies passed by Congress. The temptation to launch a series of investigations and interrogate the functioning of the Trump White House may be strong, yet congressional Democrats may wish to avoid any posturing that yields no palpable policy impact, including kicking off impeachment proceedings against Mr. Trump. A more productive way forward for Democratic lawmakers would be to engage with the White House and, through negotiation and compromise, mitigate the real impact of deleterious policies in critical areas such as health-care insurance and tariffs.

articles.title: Danger in the sewer: On India’s sewer cleaning deaths
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Despite legislation, Supreme Court orders, government programmes, the availability of mechanised cleaning technologies, and exhortations from politicians, India continues to lose sanitation workers to foreseeable, and largely preventable, circumstances. In a recent incident, four workers lost their lives in Ujjain, Madhya Pradesh , cleaning a hotel’s food-waste chamber. According to Parliament and the National Commission for Safai Karamcharis data, the number of workers who died on jobs involving sewer and septic tanks was 859 between 2014 and 2025, 498 from 2019 to mid-2026, 332 across 18 States and Union Territories in 2021-26, and 1,350 between 1993 and 2025. The figures have never tended towards zero even as the Safai Karamchari Andolan has repeatedly alleged severe under-reporting. Further, the government has maintained since at least 2021 that the practice of manually cleaning excreta from insanitary latrines has been eliminated, effectively signalling that it believes it has addressed the root of the problem when it has not, and freeing administrative bodies of the urgency of inspecting municipalities and private establishments. Members of historically marginalised castes are also overrepresented in these jobs. The law has distinguished hazardous cleaning of sewers and septic tanks from manual scavenging since 2013. Even so, persons entering them are still vulnerable to noxious gases. In Dr. Balram Singh (2023), the Court strengthened the requirements under Safai Karamchari Andolan (2014) to, among other measures, ensure outsourced sewer-cleaning contracts did not entail workers entering sewers and raise the compensation for deaths to ₹30 lakh per worker. In 2025, there was an order to end manual sewer cleaning in four metropolitan cities, Bengaluru, and Hyderabad followed a year later with notices to 15 Chief Secretaries for disobeying the 2023 order, including on the compensation.

Private contractors and municipal bodies are known to violate the restrictions on manual cleaning specified in the Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers and their Rehabilitation Act 2013 and Rules, and evade liability by hiring undocumented daily-wage workers. The scourge of such worker deaths thus cannot be eliminated without also formalising their employment and improving social security across caste lines. A significant gap between aims and outcomes has also persisted under the National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem scheme . And while it is centred on urban local bodies, its difficulties speak to the state’s fundamental error: to maximise administrative assistance, such as by distributing kits, rather than minimising the number of situations that could lead to worker deaths.

fullParagraphs: The story so far: Congress Parliamentary Party chairperson Sonia Gandhi’s memoir, Belonging: A Journey of Love , will be published in India by HarperCollins India on November 10, ending the uncertainty over its domestic release.

The book was initially expected to be published in India by Penguin Random House India (PRHI). However, PRHI announced on August 28 that it was not the publisher of the memoir in India. The announcement followed an impasse between the publisher and representatives of Ms. Gandhi over the manuscript.

articles.title: Pannun’s civil lawsuit: U.S. State Department formally serves notice on India
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: The U.S. State Department, through a diplomatic note, has formally served notice on the Government of India regarding Khalistan separatist Gurpatwant Pannun’s civil lawsuit over an alleged assassination plot.

The U.S. State Department said it was legally obliged to do so and is not taking a position on the case, adding, “The documents were delivered to the Embassy of India in Washington under cover of the U.S. Department of State note dated October 20, 2026. The diplomatic note was signed on September 30, 2026, and delivered on October 9, 2026.”

The U.S. State Department’s diplomatic note said “I, John Ballard Managing Director of the Directorate of Overseas Citizens Services, in Washington certify that this is a true copy of the United States Department of State diplomatic note signed on September 30, 2026 and delivered to the Embassy of the Republic of India in Washington DC on October 9, 2026.”

articles.title: Hyderabad gears up for Chhath Puja from November 13-16, 2026
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: While Deepavali marks the culmination of the festive celebrations for many communities across India, people from Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, Jharkhand and parts of West Bengal are preparing for another important festival — Chhath Puja . This year, large numbers of devotees are expected to gather at lakes, ponds and other water bodies across Hyderabad to offer prayers to the setting and rising Sun.

Ahead of the celebrations, the Telangana government has directed civic bodies and disaster management authorities to facilitate Chhath Puja at 28 locations across the city and make necessary arrangements, including sanitation, lighting, drinking water and crowd management. In a recent memo, the Municipal Administration and Urban Development (MAUD) department has forwarded the association’s representation to the Hyderabad Disaster Response and Asset Protection Agency (HYDRAA), and the three municipal corporations asking them to take necessary action in coordination with the departments concerned.

Chhath Puja is dedicated to the worship of the Sun God (Surya) and Chhathi Maiya. The Sun is worshipped as the source of life, energy and sustenance. Devotees offer prayers to the setting and rising Sun, seeking good health, prosperity, happiness and the well-being of their families.
Devotees offer prayers to the setting and rising Sun during Chhath Puja festival. File | Photo Credit: NAGARA GOPAL

Chhath Puja is a four-day festival, with each day having a distinct ritual. The first day, Nahay Khay, involves devotees taking a ritual bath, cleaning their homes and preparing a traditional meal. The second day, Kharna, involves a day-long fast, which is broken after sunset with offerings such as jaggery-based kheer, chapati and fruits. Following this, devotees undertake a rigorous fast without food and water.

On the third day, known as Sandhya Arghya, devotees gather at rivers, lakes, ponds and other water bodies to offer prayers to the setting Sun. Standing in water, they make offerings of fruits, sugarcane and traditional preparations. The festival concludes on the fourth day with Usha Arghya, when devotees return to the water bodies before sunrise to offer prayers to the rising Sun. The rituals conclude with devotees breaking their fast.
Chhath Puja is a four-day festival — Nahay Khay, Kharna, Sandhya Arghya and Usha Arghya — with each day having a distinct ritual. File | Photo Credit: NAGARA GOPAL

The celebrations in Hyderabad — organised by the Bihar Association, Hyderabad — are scheduled for November 14, 15 and 16. The proposed locations fall under the Greater Hyderabad Municipal Corporation (GHMC), Cyberabad Municipal Corporation (CMC) and Malkajgiri Municipal Corporation (MMC) limits. Some of the proposed locations include Tank Bund, Hasmatpet Lake, Durgam Cheruvu, Shamirpet, Miyapur and Uppal, among several others.

The association has proposed celebrations at 28 specifically named locations, apart from other Bathukamma ghats in and around the city. Tank Bund is expected to be among the major gathering points for the celebrations. “The biggest location which sees huge crowds is the Bathukamma Ghat at Tank Bund, where thousands of devotees gather to celebrate the puja. Many Ministers, legislators and retired and serving bureaucrats also participate in the celebrations here,” said Bihar Association president Hareram Singh.

The Bihar Association has urged the civic bodies to clean and maintain the designated ghats and surrounding areas, with particular attention to sanitation and hygiene. It has also sought adequate lighting at the ghats and approach roads, drinking water facilities and other essential public amenities. With devotees expected to gather for the evening prayers on November 15 and the morning rituals on November 16, the association has specifically requested adequate lighting during these periods.

Other requests include crowd management and traffic regulation in coordination with the Police Department, provision of chairs, carpets and mats, public-address systems and, wherever necessary, stages or platforms to facilitate the organised conduct of the celebrations. The association has also sought necessary safety and civic arrangements to ensure that devotees can perform the rituals in a safe, clean and orderly environment.

articles.title: Andhra government expected to make significant allocations for Neradi barrage to be constructed on Vamsadhara river
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Andhra Pradesh government is expected to make allocations in the next annual budget of the State for the year 2027-28 for the construction of Neradi barrage across Vamsadhara River and ensure dedicated water facility for nearly 2.56 lakh acres of lands in Srikakulam district of AP, which has waited nearly 55 years to overcome water dispute with the neighbouring Odisha State.

According to BRR Vamsadhara Project Chairman Aravala Ravindrababu, the State government which had given an administrative sanction for ₹461 crores a couple of months back, may give additional sanctions in the next budget. “On the request from Union Minister for Civil Aviation K. Rammohan Naidu, the Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu is keen to complete Neradi barrage within a couple of years. As a first step, it has given administrative sanction to ensure compensation for land acquisition and other needs,” said Mr. Ravindrababu while speaking to The Hindu .

Six days ago, the AP government proposed this project for optimum utilisation of water of Vamsadhara which flows nearly 82 km across Srikakulam district after flowing across 154 km in Odisha from its origin in Kalahandi district of neighbouring State. However, it was not taken up as 106 acres of land in Odisha had to be acquired for this project.

Vamsadhara Water Disputes Tribunal, which was appointed to oversee the issue, has asked AP to pay compensation for the land in Odisha and construct the project. Although the order was given in the year 2021, the Union Ministry of Water Resources has not given its nod for the project till the intervention of Mr. Chandrababu Naidu and Mr. Rammohan Naidu. As the Centre had given a notification recently, AP is all set to take up the project which might need around ₹1,099 crores. The initial allocation of ₹461 crore would ensure completion of land acquisition and beginning of the works. Mr. Ravindrababu said that the project would help farmers to grow three crops in a year in several mandals including Bhamini, Amudalavalasa, Srikakulam, Narasannapeta and others.

articles.title: Strait of Hormuz LNG traffic hits highest in October since Iran war began
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: The monthly tally of laden liquefied natural gas (LNG) tankers exiting the ​Strait of Hormuz reached its highest in October since ‌the U.S.-Iran conflict disrupted shipping this year, vessel ​tracking data showed.

* Last month, ⁠31 LNG tankers went through the key waterway, according to data from S&P Global Energy, of which ‌23 were loaded at Ras Laffan in Qatar and eight at Das Island ‌in the United Arab Emirates.
* October exports ‌were ⁠the highest since February when the war ⁠started and were up from September’s corresponding tally of 23 vessels exiting the strait, the data showed.
* “We are ​looking at UAE ‌back to pre-war transit levels and Qatar at over 30% of pre-war Hormuz transits,” said Eric Yep, a senior principal analyst at ‌S&P Global Energy.
* Kpler’s shiptracking data showed ​42 LNG cargoes were loaded in October, up from 27 in September.

* ⁠The changes come as Ras Laffan’s October loadings reached 35 cargoes, surpassing 2.7 million tons, the ‌highest since the war started, according to Kpler data. Qatar exported nearly 6.2 million tons in February.

* Two of the vessels carrying LNG from Ras Laffan that exited the strait subsequently conducted ship-to-ship (STS) transfers off the coast of ‌Oman’s Sohar anchorage, Kpler data showed. The SC Prestige ​transferred LNG to the BW ENN Crystal Sky, which is now bound for ⁠South Korea.
* The Al Mafyar moved its LNG ⁠to Shandong Redwood and Ejnan, both of which delivered the cargoes to Pakistan.
* ‌Das Island exports held steady at seven loadings in October, flat with September, Kpler ​data showed.

articles.title: RBI extends Abhyudaya Bank supersession by another year
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has extended the supersession of the board of Mumbai-based Abhyudaya Co-operative Bank Ltd. by another year, effective November 24, 2026, citing public interest.

“Upon a review, the Reserve Bank of India is satisfied that, in the public interest, it is necessary to further extend the period of supersession beyond the close of business of the bank as on November 23, 2026,” the RBI said in a circular.
The RBI first superseded the bank’s Board of Directors for one year on November 24, 2023, citing “material concerns arising from poor governance standards observed within the bank.”
The supersession, initially imposed for a year, has since been extended annually, first in November 2024, again in November 2025 and now for a further year from November 24, 2026.

With the latest extension, Mr. Satya Prakash Pathak will continue as the bank’s Administrator. He will be assisted by the existing Committee of Advisors comprising Mr. Venkatesh Hegde, Mr. Devendra Kumar and Mr. Suhas Gokhale.

fullParagraphs: The Directorate General of Hydrocarbons (DGH) on Monday extended the deadline for submitting bids for deepwater and ultra-deepwater blocks under the 10th and 11th rounds of the Open Acreage Licensing Policy (OALP) by 25 days to December 10.

The latest extension marks the seventh for the 10th round, launched in April last year, and the third for the 11th round, which opened in March this year. The deadlines were last extended in September by nearly two months to November 15.
The 10th round offers 25 blocks, including one deepwater and 12 ultra-deepwater blocks, while the 11th round has five blocks on offer, comprising one deepwater and four ultra-deepwater areas.

In August, the Union Cabinet approved an outlay of ₹84,084 crore for the Petroleum Ministry’s National Offshore Exploration Scheme, titled ‘Samudra Manthan’. The corpus, to be utilised until FY31, includes ₹43,200 crore for drilling 60 deepwater and ultra-deepwater wells.

State-owned explorers ONGC and Oil India have also announced substantial investments in offshore exploration. ONGC plans to invest ₹1 lakh crore by 2030, while Oil India has earmarked ₹15,000 crore over the next three years for deepwater and ultra-deepwater exploration.

Brent was down 84 cents, or 0.85%, to $97.48 a barrel by 0138 GMT, while West Texas Intermediate fell 32 cents, or ‌0.35%, to $90.51 a barrel.

The fall reversed minor gains made on Friday’s (November 6, 2026) settlement as the market assessed the ‌possibility of further U.S. strikes on Iran, although Brent fell ‌17% ⁠last week, the steepest weekly drop since the start ⁠of the COVID pandemic and the biggest in absolute terms, according to LSEG data dating back to 1988.
“It depends on whether or not they sign ​a very strong agreement,” Trump ‌told CNN in a phone interview. “The answer is, highly unlikely it’s going to be necessary.”

Mr. Trump had hinted at renewing attacks on Iran after last week’s U.S. midterm elections , but there has ‌been no sign of a large-scale U.S. military operation. ​Iran has said it would respond by striking U.S. and Israeli targets.

Tim Waterer, chief analyst at KCM ⁠Trade, called Mr. Trump’s comments “more measured” but said “the market is still waiting to see whether the midterms have produced a lasting shift in Trump’s ‌approach to the conflict, or whether this is just another temporary change in tone.”

Oil is headed for a glut again as recovering West Asian oil flows, rising production from other countries and weak demand have pushed global supply above consumption, JPMorgan said in a report on Friday (November 6, 2026), estimating a surplus of 1.1 million barrels ‌per day in September, widening to 1.4 million bpd in October.

He said Iraq’s losses from the Iran war and disruptions to oil exports had reached $60 ‌billion.
Separately the Houthis claimed responsibility for an attack on Saudi Aramco’s offices in the capital Riyadh on Sunday that left windows ​blown out but no reported casualties.

articles.title: Explosions heard in Saudi capital Riyadh: AFP journalists
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: Multiple explosions were heard in the Saudi capital on Tuesday (November 10, 2026), as the military coalition fighting Yemen's Houthis said it had intercepted a ballistic missile launched by the Iran-backed group towards Riyadh.
AFP journalists heard the blasts and residents received an alert on their mobile phones instructing them to take shelter due to an "aerial threat".
"Air defences intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile launched by the terrorist Houthi militia towards Riyadh," the Saudi-led coalition posted on X.
A subsequent message from the country's civil defence agency said the danger had passed.
The coalition had earlier said air defences also destroyed a ballistic missile headed towards the southern region overnight.
Saudi Arabia, the world's biggest oil exporter, has faced near-daily strikes from the Houthis for weeks, after a truce in their long-running conflict unravelled in July.
On Sunday (November 8), the Houthis claimed attacks on Riyadh's business district, where witnesses said the Aramco Tower was damaged.
Saudi authorities said the building suffered minor damage from falling shrapnel after an "attempted attack".

Images released by Saudi Arabia's press agency on Tuesday (November 10) showed the Riyadh region's deputy governor and other officials inspecting the building, with visible damage to some of its floors.
The Houthis have repeatedly targeted Aramco tankers, refineries, storage areas and the company's headquarters.
The coalition has in response been launching airstrikes against Houthi positions inside Yemen.

According to Houthi news agency Saba, Saudi warplanes on Tuesday (November 10) carried out a series of strikes on the capital Sanaa and its outskirts, targeting a gas facility and a building belonging to the Yemeni state oil company.

articles.title: Pannun’s civil lawsuit: U.S. State Department formally serves notice on India
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: The U.S. State Department, through a diplomatic note, has formally served notice on the Government of India regarding Khalistan separatist Gurpatwant Pannun’s civil lawsuit over an alleged assassination plot.

The U.S. State Department said it was legally obliged to do so and is not taking a position on the case, adding, “The documents were delivered to the Embassy of India in Washington under cover of the U.S. Department of State note dated October 20, 2026. The diplomatic note was signed on September 30, 2026, and delivered on October 9, 2026.”

The U.S. State Department’s diplomatic note said “I, John Ballard Managing Director of the Directorate of Overseas Citizens Services, in Washington certify that this is a true copy of the United States Department of State diplomatic note signed on September 30, 2026 and delivered to the Embassy of the Republic of India in Washington DC on October 9, 2026.”

On February 16, 2026, Indian citizen Nikhil Gupta had pled “guilty” at a court in New York to charges of murder, conspiracy, and money laundering to assassinate Khalistani activist Gurpatwant Singh Pannun. The government is yet to comment on the case.

According to investigators in the United States, Mr. Gupta, an Indian businessman, worked with an Indian “government employee” Vikash Yadav, believed to have been associated with India’s external intelligence agency R&AW, to hire a hitman to carry out Mr. Pannun’s murder for a total sum of $100,000. Mr. Yadav, who was arrested in December 2023 in Delhi in a separate case of kidnapping and extortion, has been out on bail since April 2024.

articles.title: How China gets the Nvidia chips it needs to develop AI
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has admitted to having an affair, reportedly with a Chinese executive at a Singapore-based company that the United States suspects of smuggling AI microchips into China.
The scandal has focused attention on how China, a major artificial-intelligence power in itself, obtains the cutting-edge chips despite US export restrictions.
Nvidia designs advanced components originally created to handle 3D visuals in video games, called Graphics Processing Units (GPUs).
These have the power to crunch colossal amounts of digital data, so are also used at scale to train and run artificial intelligence.
ChatGPT's 2022 launch showcased the potential of AI, sparking an investment gold rush as governments and tech giants raced to develop the technology further.
With chip orders pouring in, Nvidia's market valuation has soared to $4.5 trillion -- currently on par with Apple as the world's two most valuable companies.
Washington bans the export of Nvidia's top-end "Blackwell" and "Rubin" GPUs to China, citing security concerns, as advanced AI has military applications.
The policy also allows the United States's top AI labs to maintain their global lead.
Huang has lobbied the U.S. government to allow Nvidia chip sales to China, warning that the restrictions are fuelling the rise of competitive homegrown alternatives.
This year, Washington eased controls on Nvidia's previously banned -- and less powerful -- "H200" chip, with the United States taking a 25% cut of sales.
But U.S. conditions have made it difficult for shipments to be approved, with Beijing also reportedly reluctant to buy H200s as its own chip industry gains momentum.
Recent launches of high-performing models from Chinese startups, including Moonshot AI, Z.ai and DeepSeek, have turned up the heat on U.S. rivals.
